completion_condition: DB-022 records an evidence-backed decision on whether public.event_provider_connections can carry a verifiable owning-account reference, and either the additive migration that adds it with a stated predicate, or a recorded finding that the owning-account check stays purely application-side together with the named consumer that must enforce it. This handoff closes only when one of those two is recorded.
summary: The events sub-resource audit turned up an ownership boundary that no policy expresses and that one application route does not enforce. public.event_provider_connections is created by the active chain at supabase/migrations/20260927140000_event_provider_connections.sql with the comment 'Authorization for the owning ACCOUNT is not expressed in this table: owner_id is not a foreign key and the owning-account check is the application's, exactly as the archived comment records. Read access is own-rows-only.' Its four policies are all own-rows predicates on created_by: event_provider_connections_owner_read using (auth.uid() = created_by), _owner_insert, _owner_update, and a deliberate absence of any DELETE policy. So the table can say who CREATED a connection, never who the connection is FOR. app/api/events/[id]/claim/route.ts, which is in EVENTS-004's grant, was reading connections through a service-role client that bypasses those policies and was not comparing created_by to the caller, which let any authenticated caller name a stranger's owner_id and have the claim auto-approved. EVENTS-004 closed that specific path by adding .eq('created_by', user.id) to the lookup. The remaining question is not closable in application code and is the reason for this handoff: no column states the owning account, so created_by is only a proxy for control of owner_id. Two facts the database lane needs. First, the proxy is created-time, not current-time: a connection made while a user legitimately managed an account continues to read as theirs after they lose that access, and nothing in the schema expires it. Second, the writer of owner_id does not validate it: app/api/integrations/bandsintown/connect/route.ts inserts owner_type, owner_id and created_by straight from the request body with no account-ownership check. That route is outside EVENTS-004's working set and outside the database lane's, so it is named here for the orchestrator to route rather than fixed here. Exact object names: public.event_provider_connections.owner_id, public.event_provider_connections.created_by, and policies event_provider_connections_owner_read, event_provider_connections_owner_insert, event_provider_connections_owner_update. This is reported, not worked around: EVENTS-004 authored no migration, modified nothing under supabase/migrations/**, and applied nothing to any database.
completed: Read the active migration's own contract comment and recorded that the owning-account check is assigned to the application by design, not by omission.
Enumerated the four policies on public.event_provider_connections and confirmed each is an own-rows predicate on created_by, with the missing DELETE policy recorded as deliberate.
Closed the exploitable path inside the grant by binding the claim route's connection lookup to created_by, and proved the fix is load-bearing with an inverted-check run.
Identified app/api/integrations/bandsintown/connect/route.ts as an unvalidated writer of owner_id and named it for routing instead of editing outside the grant.
next_steps: DB-017 decides whether a verifiable owning-account reference can be added to public.event_provider_connections, for example a reference to the account that owner_type resolves to, and states the predicate that would make the existing own-rows policies sufficient.

If the owning-account check is to remain application-side, the decision should name the single consumer responsible for it, because the claim path and the connect path currently disagree about whether any check is required at all.

Whoever owns app/api/integrations/bandsintown/connect/route.ts should validate that the caller controls owner_id before the insert, since that is the point at which an unvalidated owner_id enters the table and every later reader inherits it.
blockers: No hosted or database verification was performed or is claimed. EVENTS-004 is forbidden from applying migrations (CP-051) and applied nothing. The claim here is about the shape of the schema as written in the migration, not about the state of any live environment.
